Bianca Buzea.bio: Bianca Buzea is Head of DevRel at Chronicle, where she works with teams integrating oracle data into onchain markets. She works directly with builders across the Ethereum ecosystem, supporting safe data infrastructure integrations tailored to different use cases. Bianca regularly speaks at blockchain events, delivering talks, workshops, and panels, including at ETHDenver, EthCC, and Dappcon.

Rangrej Ayush.bio: I’m a Computer Science student at San Francisco State University, an Ethereum Protocol Fellowship Cohort 7 fellow, and Tech Lead of the AWS student community at SFSU. I’m a full-stack generalist, but most of my work and interest is on distributed systems, data infrastructure, cloud systems, and protocol-level engineering.

YQ.bio:
Dr. YQ is the founder of AltLayer and 8004scan, scaling Ethereum with rollups and bringing agents onchain. Meanwhile, he drove the collaboration with Xfers on the stablecoin initiative for Southeast Asia StraitsX, as well as participated in blockchain projects with Mindshare, Singapore Exchange, Hg Exchange, etc.
He got his Ph.D from the National University of Singapore. His work has been published in top conferences, e.g., CCS. His work was acknowledged by Google and Apple, and media including Bitcoin Magazine, Forbes and CNBC.

Thomas Humphreys.bio: Thomas Humphreys works on the Funding Coordination team at the Ethereum Foundation, focused on capital formation and sustainable funding mechanisms that strengthen the network's long-term resilience. Previously, he was a two-time founder in identity and payments, with a background in trading, portfolio management, and security tooling.

Thomas Garrison.bio:
I am the founder of Arrow, an open-source community building
electric aircraft through on-chain coordination. A pilot and builder based on
a ranch in West Texas, where Arrow's VTOL flies commercial agricultural
work and is working towards manned aircraft.

Yoseph Ayele.bio: Yoseph is Founder & Managing Partner at LAVA, a firm that invests in founders building new financial infrastructures across Africa, researches new primitives of money, and grows builder ecosystems. He co-created Borderless Africa and magma, bringing Africa's leading founders and the Ethereum ecosystem together. He previously co-founded the Edmund Hillary Fellowship, which persuaded New Zealand to create a new visa and let a non-profit pick who came through it.

Seulkee Baek.bio: Seulkee Baek is the author of Jaune, an independent executable formal specification of Ethereum's execution layer in Lean 4, and of Blanc, a verified-compilation smart-contract stack proven against it. Contributor to ethereum/execution-specs.

Lena Hierzi.bio: Lena Hierzi is DevRel Lead at Celo Core Co, based in Lisbon. She leads a global developer relations team that accelerates cross-border payments, and she works on product management for agent infrastructure in the Celo ecosystem, including x402 payments with local stablecoins and ERC-8004 agent identity and reputation. A former hackathon builder with more than 20 wins, she has helped many developers get their first role in Web3.

Fortunato.bio: Product Lead @Kleros. He works on onchain verification, certification and decentralized dispute resolution, building tools that help ensure everyone is treated fairly. He is now bringing those same tools to the agentic economy, which needs as much fairness.

Andr\u00e1s Ar\u00e1nyi.bio: CTO at Solar Punk, where I lead our work on the agentic economy: giving AI agents on-chain identity, reputation, and payments on Ethereum and Swarm with ERC-8004 and x402. After years building decentralized applications on Swarm and aligning protocol direction with the Swarm Foundation, I focus on turning new infrastructure concepts into systems that actually run.

Lin Oshitani.bio: Lin Oshitani is a protocol researcher at Nethermind. He previously worked as a core developer of the Tezos blockchain and a software engineer at Indeed. He is currently based in Tokyo.

Gopi Mehta.bio: Gopi is a software and protocol builder working across decentralized systems, cryptography, privacy, and wallet infrastructure, with a focus on turning complex protocol ideas into systems that are easier to inspect, understand, and build with. He previously served as President and led Education & Research at TUM Blockchain Club, one of Europe’s largest student-run Web3 communities.

Vojta.bio: Vojta is a crypto native builder working on OWN, a p2p lending project focused on fixed-rate, long-term DeFi lending. He is also the lead organizer for ETHPrague 2027.

Rachit.bio: I'm Rachit Makwana, a GSoC 2026 contributor with FOSSASIA, working on Eventyay. I love exploring new technologies, solving real-world problems, and building things that make a difference. I'm passionate about open source, collaborating with developers worldwide, and turning ideas into impactful projects—one commit at a time. One of my biggest dreams is to join Google someday and build technology that impacts millions.

Harith Kamarul.bio:
Harith leads Product at Etherscan and its associated products. He has been contributing to Ethereum since 2018 by starting ETHKL, an Ethereum meetup in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia and volunteering and speaking at Devcon/nect events since then.

Before life in Ethereum, Harith worked in radio, insurance, and fintech.

Josh King.bio: Research and development engineer at Sigma Prime. Working on AI powered security vulnerability scanning and the Lighthouse consensus client.

Austin Griffith.bio: Austin Griffith. Ethereum Foundation; founder of BuidlGuidl and Scaffold-ETH. Built ethskills.com, eth-evals, and clawdbotatg, an AI agent that writes, audits and deploys its own contracts and co-hosts slop.computer.

Keating.bio: I have worked across the stack at several companies before diving into crypto in 2021 to explore problems at the intersection of privacy, economics, and software. I am currently a Lead Smart Contract Engineer at ScopeLift, which has had clients such as Compound, Optimism, Uniswap, and other major protocols.

Ben Adams.bio: Ben Adams is an Ethereum Core Developer at Nethermind, where he works on pushing the performance and scalability limits of the execution layer. He is a long-time .NET performance engineer, open-source contributor to .NET Runtime and ASP.NET Core, an 11-time Microsoft MVP, a former .NET Foundation Board Director, and co-founder and CTO of Illyriad Games.

Janmajaya Mall.bio: Inventing new cryptographic primitives at phantom.zone for a safe & resilient future. Working on new - encrypted, joint - computational mediums that are independent of the operating substrate. All-in open source!

Mateusz Morusiewicz.bio:
Day to day I'm an architect and research engineer at Flashbots: leading TEEs team, anonymous broadcast group, various MEV-related explorations.
Anonymity accelerationist, incentive aligner, CROPS maxi.

Solange Gueiros.bio: Blockchain developer, educator, and speaker, and one of the most influential voices in Brazil's crypto community. Co-founder of ETHSamba and Ethereum Brasil, with over 30 years of experience in technology, she specializes in oracles and connecting blockchains to the real world, with an MSc in digital currencies and awards across the Ethereum ecosystem.

Tomo Saito.bio: Tomo is a designer and art director at the Ethereum Foundation. Building the culture layer of the Ethereum ecosystem.

Roger Dingledine.bio: Roger Dingledine is co-founder and original developer of the Tor Project, a nonprofit that develops free and open source software to protect people from tracking, censorship, and surveillance online. Roger works with journalists and activists on many continents to help them understand and defend against the threats they face, and he is a prominent researcher in the online anonymity field.

Edmund Edgar.bio:
Free software developer based in Mashiko, Japan. 

Built the world's first smart contract oracle, Reality Keys, in 2013. Maintains reality.eth, a crowd-sourced smart contract oracle for natural language questions.

Om Vanwari.bio:
**Om Vanwari** is a Computer Science and Engineering student and an open-source software developer and contributor at **FOSSASIA**. He is a **Google Summer of Code 2026 Contributor**, where he has worked across the Eventyay ecosystem on projects involving CRM integration and video processing.

His current work focuses on **VEditor**, a standalone video review and transcoding pipeline built with FastAPI, RQ, PyAV, and PostgreSQL, designed to streamline the processing and review of conference recordings. Previously, he built and shipped **eventyay-hubspot**, integrating HubSpot CRM with Eventyay

Rose Jethani.bio: Rose is a ZK and protocol engineer at Atheon, working on ProveKit, cryptographic optimization, and Trinity. Previously, she worked on MEV infrastructure at Primev, applied cryptography at ZK Email, and Ethereum protocol research through Nethermind and the Ethereum Protocol Fellowship. She also contributes to Prysm, Reth, and rust-libp2p.

Hart Montgomery.bio: Hart Montgomery is the CTO of Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust and serves as the ED of the Post-Quantum Cryptography Alliance. Hart previously worked in blockchain and cryptography research at Fujitsu where he helped lead Fujitsu’s efforts in Hyperledger. Prior to Fujitsu, Hart received a Ph.D. in cryptography at Stanford. Hart has numerous academic publications and patents in cryptography and blockchain and brings a wealth of experience in these areas to the LF.

A blockchain engineer from Vietnam who is always curious and eager to learn. 
I hope that one day my work can make a meaningful impact on the blockchain ecosystem.

Gustavo Dutra.bio: Gustavo Dutra is a Security Engineer at Polygon Labs building agentic security tooling — AI code review in CI, autonomous bounty triage, and supply-chain auditing. His background spans C++ software engineering, web2 security, and red teaming.

Shinya Mori.bio: Since 2022, he has worked on researching public goods funding mechanisms though quantitative comparative analysis of various grant programs. In 2023, he co-founded Fracton Research (Beacon Labs). He has spoken at Devcon SEA and Funding the Commons Bangkok and Buenos Aires. He was a member of Grant Innovation Lab by Metagov and Polygon Community grant council. In 2024, he co-founded imi and began his artistic practice. He co-organizes kuu village for alternative lives leveraged by Ethereum.

Manu Sheel Gupta.bio: Manu Sheel Gupta is building LeakDetectAI and is a Technical Lead and maintainer across libp2p, multiformats, and IPLD, working on P2P networking, secure communication channels, PQ clients interoperability, decentralized systems, and open Internet infrastructure. His work focuses on secure, resilient, and permissionless networks through open standards, security research, and open-source development. He is a volunteer and contributes to the Trillion Security Research (1TS) initiative at Ethereum.

haurog.bio: Physicist, programmer, cypherpunk, optimistic pessimist and believer in public goods. Running and testing client software since before the beacon chain genesis.

0xRajeev.bio: Rajeev is the founder of Secureum where he dedicates his time to scaling Ethereum security, after having spent >25 years doing security research. He is a Cantina Fellow & Lead Security Researcher at Spearbit, and has previously collaborated with Trail of Bits (as one of the leading contributors to Slither). He has a PhD in CS, with a focus on cybersecurity, from Purdue University, USA. He spent seven years at Intel USA as a security architect and strategist.

Josselin Feist.bio: Josselin Feist is a security researcher at Aave, where he leads the onchain risk effort. Previously, he was Engineering Director of the Blockchain team at Trail of Bits. He is the creator of Slither, the widely used Solidity static analysis framework, and holds a PhD in software vulnerability analysis. His work spans smart contracts, L1/L2 protocols, bridges, and core blockchain infrastructure, with a focus on systemic risks, protocol design, and security strategy.

P\u00e9ter Szil\u00e1gyi.bio: Peter has been working in the Ethereum ecosystem for about a decade, since then he's trying to build something similar in the world of genomics.

Anamarija.bio: Communications Lead at TheDAO Security Fund

Sem Bloom.bio: Sem is a hacker and Ethereum security researcher with roots in the early cypherpunk movement. An early DarkWallet contributor and creator of EVMcrispr, he has spent over a decade exploring the boundaries of decentralized systems, from privacy-preserving wallets and DAO governance to smart contract security, EVM scripting and simulation, and unconventional onchain fund recovery.

Elliot Friedman.bio: Elliot is a smart contract security engineer and principal at Solidity Labs. Over seven years he has deployed 67 production contracts securing more than $2 billion in TVL, with zero losses. He built Forge Proposal Simulator, a governance security tool widely adopted across DeFi, and Kleidi, a timelock-based self-custody system built to defend against attacks that multisigs can't stop. A contributor to SEAL Frameworks, he writes and speaks on smart contract and governance security.

Federico Ast.bio: Federico Ast is the founder and CEO of Kleros, a decentralized dispute resolution protocol built on Ethereum. He holds degrees in Economics and Philosophy and a doctorate in Business Management, and teaches blockchain and the future of law to over 120,000 students on Coursera. His work sits at the intersection of blockchain, game theory, institutional design, legaltech, and AI.

Mukund.bio: I'm a software developer and open-source contributor from India. Also, a Google Summer of Code 2026 contributor with FOSSASIA, working on TeamShifts, a team and volunteer management plugin for the Eventyay platform. I've been contributing to FOSSASIA for 9 months now. Alongside open source, I'm interested in software development, AI, and building practical technology projects. Through GSoC, I have explored what it means to work on a real-world project with an existing codebase and an international open-source community.

Saksham Sirohi.bio:
I’m a software engineer and open-source maintainer working across large-scale web applications, AI systems, real-time communication, and data-driven software. I’ve built and maintained production systems across the frontend and backend, working with technologies including Django, Vue, TypeScript, WebRTC, WebSockets, and modern AI/ML tooling.
Alongside systems engineering, I work on AI-powered software and developer tooling, including LLM applications, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, and evaluation pipelines.

Bas van Gijzel.bio: Bas van Gijzel is an Engineering Manager at Nomic Foundation, leading work across Solidity compiler and language tooling, including Slang and solx. His broader background spans developer tooling, compilers, and engineering leadership, with a focus on making complex systems faster, safer, and easier to use.

Ula\u015f Erdo\u011fan.bio:

Subhra Mazumdar.bio: Subhra Mazumdar is an Assistant Professor in the Department of CSE, Indian Institute of Technology Indore. Before that, she was a post-doctoral researcher in the Security and Privacy (S&P) Research Unit at Vienna University of Technology, Austria, where she worked on rational attacks on Layer 2 protocols in Blockchain. She did both Ph.D. and M.tech in Computer Science from Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata, in 2022 and 2018, respectively.

polymutex.bio: polymutex works on Walletbeat, and wants wallets to actually reflect the cypherpunk ethos of crypto.

Vivek Singh Solanki.bio: Vivek Singh Solanki is an Ethereum Protocol Fellow (cohort 7) working on go-ethereum, where he is building core/ssz: SSZ encoding and decoding, progressive merkleization and proof generation, as groundwork for EIP-7807 SSZ execution blocks. He is based in India.

Jack.bio: Jack is a graduate student and Ethereum Protocol Fellowship (EPF7) participant focused on Ethereum protocol development. His fellowship project explores the foundations for EIP-7807 SSZ execution blocks in Erigon, including execution-data mapping, progressive SSZ Merkleization, and block-root computation. He has contributed to Ethereum's execution-specs repository and participated in the LXDAO and ETHPanda communities. His interests include execution-layer infrastructure, verifiable data access, and open-source collaboration.

Chibuotu Amadi.bio: Chibuotu Amadi is co-founder of Paycrest, where he works on open infrastructure for stablecoin–fiat payments. He has spent 7+ years building in crypto, including at ConsenSys and Gitcoin, with work spanning cross-chain systems and public-goods tooling. He now focuses on making the fiat edge of crypto more open, verifiable, and non-custodial.

Mudit Gupta.bio: Mudit is the Chief Technology Officer at Polygon. He's a security researcher by the day and an ethereum developer by the night.

Pablo Sabbatella.bio:

Julia Hardy.bio: Julia is the Co-Founder and Head of Investigations of zeroShadow, a holistic web3 security solution service created to enable crypto companies to enhance their security and incident response capabilities. Julia also serves as a volunteer for SEAL911.

Georgy Kobakhidze.bio: A senior partner at Consensys Diligence, George is fascinated by Math, Technology, and their human aspects - privacy, game theory, digital identity, and so on. Eventually he found Ethereum, a promising world that fit his interests, where he focuses on security to safeguard the future of finance.

Jon Stephens.bio: Jon Stephens is the CEO and co-founder of Veridise, a blockchain security company specializing in audits and security tooling for smart contracts, blockchain systems, and zero-knowledge technologies. He is also a computer science PhD student at UT Austin, where his research focuses on formal methods, program analysis, verification, and security.

Shankara Pailoor.bio: I am the CRO of Veridise, a blockchain company specializing in securing smart contracts, infrastructure, and zero-knowledge technologies. I graduated from UT Austin with a PhD in Computer Science, specializing in programming languages and formal methods.

Antonio Seveso.bio:
I've been involved full-time in the blockchain space since 2020, but experimenting with the tech on a personal level since 2013, mostly on privacy-focused solutions.
With a full-stack background, I define myself a solidity dev with an architectural view when it comes to develop applications in Web3. Currently I'm the Co-founder of Fluidkey, bringing default-privacy with great UX on EVMs.
Outside blockchain space, I'm a basketball lover, LEGO nerd and roller-coaster enthusiast.

Dmytro Matviiv.bio: Dmytro Matviiv is the CEO of HackenProof, expert bug bounty and crowdsourced audit platform working with crypto leaders such as Ethereum Foundation, MetaMask, Polygon, OKX, SUI and more. ETHSecurity Expert Badge holder with 15 years in data encryption, authentication and developing cybersecurity products. Specializes in evidence validation, threat attribution, and collaborative intelligence. Nowadays, HackenProof consists of a community of over 80K security researchers.

Vaibhav Chhabra.bio: Vaibhav Chhabra is a Mechanical Engineer turned Carpenter and Educator. With a degree from Boston University, Vaibhav spent his early career at EyeNetra, a startup from MIT Media Labs, building portable Virtual Reality-based eye diagnostic devices. During his time in India for the eye diagnostic prototype, he recognized the need for accessible makerspaces and founded Makers Asylum in 2013 out of a small garage in Mumbai. Simon Jentzsch.bio: Simon Jentzsch has worked on Ethereum since 2015, focused on verification and trust-minimized access. He authored EIP-1186 (eth_getProof) — the account and storage proof widely used by light clients. Formerly co-founder and CTO of Slock.it and lead contributor to the Incubed light client, he is now co-founder and CTO of corpus.core and main contributor to colibri-stateless, a stateless Ethereum verifier.

Abhimanyu Nag.bio: Abhimanyu is a MITACS Fellow in Mathematics at the University of Alberta. He holds a BSc from the University of Alberta and has worked in Security, Risk and Consensus with Nethermind, Pantera Backed TanX, Catalysis Labs as well as Antler's Chainrisk Labs as Chief Scientist. His research has been published by IEEE, Springer, and Financial Cryptography, and he was cited in the Ethereum Research Paper at the age of 20 for EIP 5133. His main work is in the intersection of cryptography and economics.

Luiz Vasconcelos.bio: Luiz is an Open Source Developer at OpenZeppelin, working on solidity libraries, such as the main openzeppelin-contracts and the Open Intents Framework.

Jacob Czepluch.bio:
I've been working on Ethereum for 11 years. Spanning from the Python Ethereum client, to payment channels (Raiden Network), to security tooling at Phylax Systems and now contributing to the Solidity language.
On the side, I've organized the Copenhagen Ethereum Meetup for almost 11 years and have been part of DoD in Berlin, organizing EthBerlin and Protocolberg.

Hudson Jameson.bio: Hudson is a renowned expert on blockchain technology with specializations in Ethereum, Zcash, decentralized governance, and privacy technology. He has spoken at dozens of conferences around the world and has served at a number of organizations and boards, including advisory roles at Chainlink and Polygon. As a community builder and educator, his unique mix of technical and communication skills has proved to be valuable in ecosystems that he participates in.

James Newell.bio: James Newell has spent nearly 20 years working with charities and social purpose businesses as a fundraiser, founder, consultant, executive, and non-executive director. He now works at GSR, a crypto market maker and liquidity provider with over a decade in the ecosystem, where he leads the firm's sustainability commitment and is building the GSR Foundation into a leading independent charitable grantmaker.

Diego Siqueira.bio: Diego is a staff engineer at Zircuit. He uses Go to build secure and reliable distributed systems. His work covers Ethereum infrastructure, protocol security, rollups, and reproducible failure and recovery tests.

Kevin Jones.bio:
Kevin is the Founder of an AI Security startup called 1Claw, focused on security, guardrails and agentic commerce.

He is also a core member of the BuidlGuidl, where he educates developers all over the world about Ethereum.

Cl\u00e9ment Lesaege.bio: Clément is a computer scientist and founder of Kleros, a decentralized arbitration protocol for smart contracts. His work spans mechanism design, game theory, smart contract security, and decentralized coordination. Beyond Kleros, he has worked on Sybil-resistant systems like Proof of Humanity and on prediction and decision markets through Seer. He is interested in markets for governance, funding, risk, and collective decision-making. Outside work, Clément plays competitive Magic: The Gathering.

Artem B..bio:
Artem is deeply passionate about decentralized technology and its ability to empower people with censorship resistance, personal sovereignty, privacy, and permissionless innovation. Focused in the area of Public Goods, Decentralized Identity and Civic Tech.
He is a a builder at heart and a technology leader with experience across many industries over the last 15 years.

cvh.bio: Christopher is the Head of Security at Polygon Labs. His background spans SaaS, cloud security, blockchain, AI, operational efficiency, and software development. Luca Donno.bio: Head of Research at L2BEAT. Working on specifications to enable native rollups on Ethereum. I like CROPS.

Chris Hobcroft.bio: Chris Hobcroft has worked on Ethereum-related projects since 2017. He now builds deboot, a bootloader that fetches its operating system from Swarm and verifies it against signatures from the same keys that control funds, an attempt to close the last centralised gap underneath a self-hosted node. He also contributes to Ethereum, Livepeer and Swarm communities.

Rohit M S.bio:
Rohit M S is an AWS Certified Solutions Architect and DevOps/Backend Engineer with over 8 years of experience building and automating cloud infrastructure. His expertise spans the full DevOps lifecycle — CI/CD pipeline design with Jenkins, GitHub, Docker, and Kubernetes, plus infrastructure-as-code using Terraform and Ansible across AWS and Azure. Mark Holt.bio: I am a life long software developer who hase been working on various blockchain projects since 2016, I have been a core member of the Erigon team since 2023.

Csaba.bio:
Csaba is a member of the Geth team and a researcher at the EF. His current focus is on hardening and scaling the Ethereum networking stack, mempool and DAS.
Previously, he was working on various aspects of overlay and mesh networks, from large scale P2P overlays for low-latency video streaming, through anonymization overlays and other privacy enhancing technologies, to wireless mesh networks of all kinds. He has 50+ published papers and he is holding several IEEE Best Paper and Best Demo awards.

Karam Alhamad.bio: Karam Alhamad is a Syrian-German builder of public infrastructure for open societies, and an Ethereum Foundation Next Billion Fellow (2022-23). A political detainee under Assad, stripped of his ID papers, he left Syria in 2014. He founded ZeFi Foundation, his open-source umbrella, and its flagship Nawafith is the open civic register of the Syrian state, built between Berlin and Damascus with Syrian civil-society partners and shipped as an Arabic-first kit others can replicate.

Otto Kekalainen.bio: An open source enthusiast with a long background in Linux systems administration, high-availability databases and fan of distributed systems. Currently work as an independent consultant developing Debian and Ubuntu. On the side tinkering with with RISC-V hardware for local AI inference and writing about tech and strategy at optimizedbyotto.com.

Soumyadip Chowdhury.bio: Soumyadip is a Senior Software Engineer at Redhat with a passion for technology and knowledge sharing. With previous experience at HoiChoi Technologies and Bajaj Finserv, he brings a diverse background to his role. Soumyadip has actively participated in over 100 online and offline events as a speaker. His expertise extends to the domains of DTN (Delay Tolerant Networking) and Blockchain, where he has contributed by writing book chapters and journals. Soumyadip is known for his dedication to helping fellow tech enthusiasts enhance their skills, making him a valuable resource in the community.

Hugo Volz Oliveira.bio:
Hugo serves as Partnerships Lead at ScopeLift, a full-stack EVM-focused software engineering
studio which also developed Umbra Cash and operates Cactus (formerly known as Tally) Ethereum's first stealth addresses project. 

Hugo is also the co-founder and secretary at New Economy Institute, an advocacy group focused on
making Portugal and Europe more crypto friendly, having led the negotiations with the Portuguese
government for the friendly crypto taxation regime implemented in 2023.

Steffen Kux.bio: Steffen is Co-Founder and Co-CEO of corpus.core, focusing on trustless blockchain infrastructure, stateless verification, and privacy-preserving client architectures. With more than 25 years of experience in software architecture and distributed systems, he has been building blockchain infrastructure since the early Ethereum ecosystem. He coordinates the development & application of colibri, an open-source stateless client for trustless blockchain verification.

Dirk J\u00e4ckel.bio: Dirk is a Berlin-based Android developer who has been building apps since 2009 and following Ethereum since 2015. From 2020 to 2023 he was a mobile developer at Gnosis and Safe, working on the Safe{Wallet} mobile apps. He is the creator and maintainer of Myotis, an open-source light client that gives mobile and desktop apps trustless access to Ethereum without relying on RPC providers.

Zaryab.bio:
A smart contract engineer and researcher at Push Chain, working at the intersection of AI and blockchains.

Edu.bio: Eduardo Antuña is a software engineer and protocol builder with 9 years of experience in Ethereum, zero-knowledge technology, and decentralized infrastructure. Francesco Risitano.bio: Francesco Risitano is a research engineer working on Ethereum scalability and privacy. He has worked across the stack, including zkVM development at Polygon Miden, node client development at Scroll, and now at the Ethereum Foundation, where he works on Ethereum’s transition to execution proofs.

Levi Katyal Sledd.bio: Levi Katyal Sledd is a blockchain security researcher at OpenZeppelin whose interests include cryptography, arithmetic circuits, and zero-knowledge proofs.  Ph.D. Math, Vanderbilt University.

Daniel Knopik.bio:

Eric DeCourcy.bio:

Her interests include statistical simulation, time-series data mining, network science, and applications of Machine Learning to finance and economics. She previously worked in the fields of fraud detection and cybercrime.

Lexa Lyu.bio: Yijian "Lexa" Lyu is a PhD researcher in Religious Studies at the University of Iowa. Kati Illes.bio: Frontier Tech and Web3 product/project management for UNICEF's Ventures and Cryptofund - responsible for Web3 prototypes and pilots at the intersection of humanitarian fintech and digital public goods.

Arun Maharajan.bio:

Office of Innovation. He was instantly drawn to blockchains as they promised to

ecosystems to enable pilots/PoCs/projects for positive outcomes in social,
humanitarian, financial and economic spheres. He has special interests in new

world meets Web3.

Nicolas Garcia.bio: Security researcher at OpenZeppelin, where I have spent the last five-plus years auditing some of the leading protocols in the ecosystem.

Dominic Bruetsch.bio: Dominic Bruetsch is a founding partner and lead blockchain security engineer at ChainSecurity. He specializes in smart contract audits on Ethereum, Starknet, as well as  zk circuit audits. He holds a master's degree from ETH Zurich, one of the best universities in the world for computer science, in electrical engineering with a focus on networks and computer science. He found vulnerabilities in the Ethereum protocol itself, which landed him a sport on the Ethereum Bug bounty leaderboard.

Chiranjeev Mishra.bio: I'm a software engineer at Inco Network working on privacy and cryptography infrastructure. I authored ERC-8286 and contributed to EIP-8141, love working in open source (oss at Safe Global, Viem, eip8141)

Qiang Zhu.bio: Qiang Zhu brings a wealth of experience in application development to his role as Head of Engineering. He previously served as Director of Engineering at Camera360, a leading image and video mobile application company, and as a Tech Lead at Adobe, where he contributed to one of the industry's most widely used software solutions. He is also the co-author of EIP-6821 and co-founder of Web3Builder.tech, with active contributions to the Ethereum ecosystem.

Suraj Shetty.bio: I build tools for people who build things. At Frappe, that's Frappe Builder, the open source website builder I started in 2022 because I wanted something simple, fast, and nice to use. It now runs [frappe.io](http://frappe.io), which still feels a little surreal.

Darryl Yeo.bio:
Darryl Yeo is a self-taught software engineer with over a decade of experience building delightful data-driven experiences for the decentralized web. He previously built websites and user interfaces at dYdX, Ritual, ETHGlobal, Spindl and Coinbase.

Today, Darryl focuses on building open-source tools that promote transparency and self-sovereignty in crypto ecosystems, including Walletbeat, a community standard for Ethereum wallets, and Blockhead, a local-first client for decentralized protocols.

hpdang.bio:
Hong Phuc Dang is the founder of FOSSASIA, a driving force behind the open source movement across Asia. Since 2009, she has brought together developers, contributors, and communities through the annual [FOSSASIA Summit](https://summit.fossasia.org), one of Asia’s leading open source events.

Hong Phuc has served on the boards of the Open Source Initiative (OSI), the Open Source Business Alliance, and IEEE Open Source. She works with organizations to adopt open source and InnerSource practices, helping build more open, collaborative, and innovative technology ecosystems.

Mike McCabe.bio: I want private money for public chains and therefore I've been building Privacy Pools for the last two years.

Atharva Mhaske.bio: Atharva Mhaske is a Backend Engineer at Cloud9 and an Open Source Member at OpenEverest, where he leads work on provider-kserve with LLM inferecing on K8s. He was a Google Summer of Code mentee at OpenScienceLabs. His work spans backend systems, applied AI engineering, and AI infrastructure on Kubernetes.

Yuting Jiang.bio: Yuting is the co-founder and CEO of Agora Citizen Network, an open-source collective intelligence tool that helps people map opinions and build consensus on complex issues. Agora has been used by institutions and NGOs like UNESCO and Search for Common Ground (peacebuilding). She also organizes future imagination workshops and designs participatory processes.

Mikel Cortes.bio: Currently working as a Software and Research Engineer at ProbeLab, he used to work at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center and MigaLabs, while he was awarded a PhD research fellowship from Protocol Labs. During the fellowship he had the opportunity to collaborate on various research projects with entities like Protocol Labs, the Filecoin Foundation, the Ethereum Foundation, the University of Cambridge, and the Codex Storage team at Status.

Manuel Wedler.bio: Manuel is a member of Argot Collective, an Ethereum Foundation spin-out working on compilers and developer tooling, where he builds source-code verification infrastructure for the Sourcify project. Most recently his focus has been Onay, a local signing companion that verifies transactions on your own device, and the Ethereum Foundation’s Clear Signing Initiative, where he co-maintains the open descriptor registry and develops an ERC-7730 decoding library. He has worked in the Ethereum ecosystem since 2018, on open-source projects such as Raiden Network and Beamer Bridge.

Yash Saraswat.bio: I like math and cryptography. I work as a software engineer at ether.fi and was an ethereum protocol fellow. I believe ethereum will bring global finance on-chain.

Jimin Lee.bio: Studying and building in tech, culture and statecraft: popups, communities, startup societies, new cities, networks.

Facundo Trotz.bio: I'm a lawyer with several years of experience advising on blockchain and decentralized systems. Currently, I work for Kleros Cooperative, where I lead policy design and government initiatives to integrate the Kleros protocol into the public sector.

Bartho Laforestrie.bio: I am a researcher in philosophy at École normale supérieure–PSL, affiliated with the Archives Husserl laboratory. My research examines blockchain infrastructures, algorithmic intentionality, and the distribution of responsibility in decentralized systems, with a particular focus on Ethereum.

Nicolas Assouad.bio: Nicolas Assouad is Tech Lead at Spiko, which operates Europe's largest tokenized regulated funds infrastructure across more than five EVM networks, as well as Starknet, Stellar, and Solana. He builds the multi-chain infrastructure behind these funds, including the event archival system born from Spiko's regulatory obligation to keep fund history queryable even after a network shuts down, and authors Spiko's engineering deep-dives.

Tomoki Adachi.bio: Engineer at Nyx Foundation. Previously, I was responsible for product development in the cross-chain space. At Nyx, I am involved in protocol implementation and verifiable system design.

Johanna Moran.bio: I'm Strategy and Operations Lead for libp2p, the P2P networking stack underpinning IPFS, Filecoin, Ethereum, and Polkadot, and co-founder of Meshworks alongside Manu Sheel Gupta. My work spans ecosystem sustainability, grant-making, funding strategy, partnerships, and standards engagement for libp2p under the Open Impact Foundation. I represent libp2p at the IETF, where our team's work on verifiable telemetry for large-scale deployments was recently accepted at IETF 126 Vienna.

Artem Grigor.bio: Artem Grigor is a DPhil candidate in the Systems Security Lab at the University of Oxford

Mo Jahanara.bio: I am a member of the writes team in access layer at EF. I work on bringing more robust privacy and censorship resistance to the Ethereum!

James Carnley.bio: James Carnley builds cypherpunk public infrastructure and created Ethereum File System, an open-source public good providing a shared global namespace, reliable onchain metadata and verifiable file references on Ethereum. He spent more than a decade building federated medical software at Epic and has been active in Ethereum since 2017 through beacon chain testnets and staking discussions. He now develops EFS and is designing a user-sovereign web operating system.

Patrick Storchenegger.bio: Patrick Storchenegger is managing Partner at PST Legal in Switzerland, advising blockchain projects and developers on liability and regulatory questions. He has more than 20 years of experience at the intersection of law, finance and emerging technology. He advises crypto clients on crypto-asset regulation, tax, corporate matters, and cross-border compliance. He serves on the boards of several blockchain entites.

Raphael Baumann.bio: Raphael Baumann is a partner at PST Legal & Consulting in Zug, where he co-leads the firm's Emerging Technologies & Artificial Intelligence practice. He advises since more than 8 years Web3 projects on DLT, DeFi and digital-asset regulation, and has guided numerous token offerings, DeFi structures and DAOs from concept through regulatory assessment.

Dr Sujit Prakash Gujar.bio: Dr. Sujit Gujar is an Associate Professor and CA Technologies Faculty Chair at IIIT Hyderabad, leading the Machine Learning Lab. His research develops game-theoretic foundations for modern AI and distributed AI/blockchains, ensuring fairness in these systems, spanning 125+ peer-reviewed publications and 15+ US patents. He earned his Ph.D. from the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, winning the IISc Alumni Medal for best CSA thesis, and previously researched at EPFL and Xerox Research.

Henning Diedrich.bio: Henning is the protocal lead at Swarm and creator of the open-source, human-readable smart contract language Lexon.
